tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After moving the largest disk that is not yet in its final position onto its goal peg, treat the remaining smaller disks as a subproblem and solve recursively.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest unsolved disk can be placed on its target peg without violating any rule.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a small disk onto a peg that still needs a larger disk later, causing a block.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg using the third peg as auxiliary, first move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk to the target, and finally move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a clean stack of consecutive disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while smaller disks remain on top of it, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer must be a single syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last parseable list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, before any trailing whitespace.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including extra commentary after the list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally replay each move from the initial state and confirm that the resulting arrangement matches the goal before submitting.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move sequence, before final output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, resulting in a mismatched final configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should contain only the move list; any additional characters or commentary may be interpreted as part of the list and cause parsing errors.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Adding a trailing period after the list, which the parser treats as invalid syntax.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the source peg’s top disk matches the moving disk and that the destination peg’s top (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence, for every move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one, which violates the Tower of Hanoi rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you intend to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 onto peg 2 while disks 2 and 1 are still on that peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk on a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, because the small disk would block the larger one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto peg 0 and then later trying to place disk 5 onto the same peg without moving disk 1 away first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate the smaller disks above it to any other peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk that has smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 4 is on top of it, making the move illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place small onto larger only if larger is already final
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When stacking a smaller disk onto a larger one, ensure the larger disk will not be moved again (i.e., it is already in its final position); otherwise the smaller disk would block the larger disk’s later movement.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a small disk onto a peg that already contains a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting disk 1 onto peg 0 while disk 5 is still on that peg and will later need to be moved off, causing a blockage.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves or forgets to include the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always construct and output a non‑empty list of moves, even if it is just a placeholder that will be replaced later.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation is cut off early, leaving the list unfinished or missing closing brackets.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the move list is fully written and syntactically complete before ending the response.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk without checking the current stack order on the source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before adding a move, verify that the chosen disk is the top element of its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model places a small disk on the goal peg before larger disks that need to be underneath have been moved there.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Clear the target peg of any smaller disks before moving larger ones onto it, and only place small disks onto the goal peg after all larger required disks are already in place.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not check the size relationship between the moving disk and the destination peg’s top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing the move.
